body:
Chloe Martin: PR up for suggestions-service read API routes + tenant scoping. Would love eyes today so we can land before Console BFF hooks it up. https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18642

Chloe Martin: Summary:
- `GET /suggestions` list w/ basic filtering (route, model, region)
- `GET /suggestions/{id}` detail
- tenant scoping via workspace_id from auth context
- response includes `savings_estimate` + `risk` (fields coming from downstream)

Felix Schneider: taking a look now. quick q: is schema versioning in this PR or follow-up? I don’t see `schema_version` on the payload.

Chloe Martin: follow-up. Trying to keep this PR minimal to unblock UI plumbing. ENG-2410 is versioned schema.

Jada Williams: ok but we should at least avoid painting ourselves into a corner. if the UI starts depending on fields that will change, we’ll have breakage. can we add a top-level `payload_version: "v1"` now even if it’s just a constant?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 from authz/tenancy side: want to confirm we never accept tenant/workspace as a query param. only derive from session.

Chloe Martin: yep, no query param for tenant. using `ctx.tenant.workspaceId`.

Ines Carvalho: looking at filters: `route_id` is passed as query param though. that’s fine, but are we verifying route_id belongs to the tenant before using it in DB query?

Chloe Martin: good catch. currently we filter suggestions by `workspace_id` first, then optional `route_id` filter. so worst case it just returns empty.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: as long as workspace_id is enforced in the WHERE clause, ok.

Felix Schneider: one more: on list endpoint, `limit` default 50, max 200. cursor/pagination not here. is that ok for beta tenants?

Chloe Martin: for now yes. pagination is in PR 18714. (not blocked on that for small cohort)

Logan Wright: on schema: can we make sure the list response includes a stable identifier we can use for telemetry events? like `suggestion_id` (uuid) and `suggestion_type`.

Chloe Martin: list includes `id`, `type`, `created_at`, `applies_to` (route/model/region), and `status`. detail includes explanations.

Nadia Rahman: can you paste an example response? I want to sanity check the `baseline`/`estimated` naming before it leaks into docs.

Chloe Martin: sure, from staging:
```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "sugg_01HP9J...",
      "type": "enable_prefix_cache",
      "status": "active",
      "applies_to": {
        "route_id": "route_8f2...",
        "model": "mistral-7b-instruct",
        "region": "us-east"
      },
      "risk": {
        "level": "medium",
        "rationale": ["Latency headroom < 15% at p95", "Workload variance high (p90/p50 > 2.3x)"]
      },
      "savings_estimate": {
        "currency": "USD",
        "period": "30d",
        "estimated_savings_usd": 412.55,
        "estimated_savings_usd_ci90": "[210.12, 590.04]",
        "estimated_savings_per_1m_tokens_usd": 3.18,
        "confidence": "0.72"
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null
}
```
(note: `next_cursor` is always null in this PR, will become real when cursor pagination lands)

Nadia Rahman: ah, `estimated_savings_usd_ci90` as a stringified range is a bit :grimacing:. is that coming from downstream? ADR-0275 wanted numeric bounds.

Jada Williams: yeah, ADR-0275 had `ci_lower`/`ci_upper` numeric. Can we align now? otherwise we’re gonna have a cleanup PR across service + UI.

Chloe Martin: that range string is just from my local fixture; real service returns `ci_lower_usd` / `ci_upper_usd`. I’ll update the example + ensure types are numeric.

Allison Grant: also please add a note in code comment where `confidence` is 0-1 float, not “low/med/high”. i’ve seen dashboards break on this.

Felix Schneider: review note: in `SuggestionsController.list()` we’re returning `applies_to` as an object. are we ok with that given our “no nested” preference for analytics events? (not blocking, just thinking ahead)

Logan Wright: for analytics we can flatten when emitting events (`route_id`, `model`, `region`). API can stay nested.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: security nit: ensure audit logging is not in this PR (or if it is, make sure it doesn’t log query params like model name). cost/usage-derived data can be sensitive.

Chloe Martin: audit logging is separate PR (18695). This PR only does RBAC check + tenant scoping.

Ines Carvalho: 👍 overall. request: add explicit 404 vs 403 behavior. if user tries to fetch suggestion id not in tenant, return 404 (not 403) to avoid enumeration.

Chloe Martin: makes sense. currently returns 404 when `workspace_id` doesn’t match. will add a test.

Felix Schneider: left comments on PR about naming (`payload_version`), and a small refactor to centralize query parsing.

Chloe Martin: saw them. I’ll push an update:
- add `payload_version: "v1"` top-level (constant)
- numeric CI bounds + clarify confidence
- test for 404 on cross-tenant id

Connor O'Brien: (release) if this lands today, can we tag it for tomorrow’s train? we’re trying to keep Console beta behind flag but want endpoints in prod.

Chloe Martin: yep, once approvals in, I’ll merge and ping you.

Redwood CI Bot: build passed on commit 9f3c2b1 (unit tests, lint) 

Jada Williams: re-reviewing latest commit now.

Jada Williams: looks good with `payload_version` + ci bounds. approving.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: approving as well. thanks for the 404 test.

Ines Carvalho: approved.

Chloe Martin: merged. thanks all. will link this in ENG-2402 + ping Console folks.

Logan Wright: please drop a note in #eng once BFF starts emitting `suggestion_viewed` events so we can confirm id/type fields match.

Chloe Martin: will do.
